Rows that span from col 2 to col 10!
Cols that span from row 1 to row 9!
Wait, in Ex 1:

Row 1 and 9 are the horizontal borders!

Row 1 to 6, Col 1 to 6!

No interior lines!
Just a single rectangle!

Wait, why are some lines considered lines?
Look at how the lines are drawn:
They are dashed/dotted lines of the same color!
A line is defined if:
Between the bounding box limits, there are pixels along that row/col.

No, in Ex 1:
Row 3 has pixels at col 2, 5, 7. But it is NOT completed into a line!
Why? Because row 3 is not a line!
Why is Row 4 in Ex 2 a line, but Row 3 in Ex 1 not a line?
Look at Ex 2:
Row 4 has 4s at cols 2,3, 5, 7,8, 10. That's 6 pixels out of 9!

Row 5 has 4 at col 2. (only 1 pixel)

Row 9 has 4 at cols 2, 4,5, 7,8,9. (6 pixels out of 9)
Notice: The lines that are drawn have majority of pixels (or > 50% or >= threshold)?
Wait, look at row 7 in Ex 2:
It has 6 pixels, row 9 has 6 pixels, row 4 has 6 pixels, row 1 has 7 pixels.
All line rows have >= 6 pixels!
Other rows have at most 2 pixels!
In Ex 1:
Columns:
Col 2: 5 pixels out of 7 (rows 2,3, 5,6, 8)
Col 5: 6 pixels out of 7 (rows 2,3,4, 6,7, 8)
Col 7: 5 pixels out of 7 (rows 2,3, 5,6, 8)
Col 9: 5 pixels out of 7 (rows 2, 4,5, 7,8)
Other columns: col 3 has 1, col 4 has 1, col 6 has 1, col 8 has 2!
Rows in Ex 1:
Row 2: 6 pixels out of 8
Row 8: 6 pixels out of 8
Other rows: at most 3 pixels out of 8!
In Ex 3:
Bounding box: rows 1..6 (length 6), cols 1..6 (length 6).
Row 1: cols 1,2, 4, 6 -> 4 pixels out of 6
Row 6: cols 1, 3,4, 6 -> 4 pixels out of 6
Other rows: row 2 (1 pixel), row 3 (1 pixel), row 4 (2 pixels), row 5 (1 pixel).
Col 1: rows 1, 3,4, 6 -> 4 pixels out of 6
Col 6: rows 1,2, 4,5,6 -> 5 pixels out of 6
Other cols: at most 2 pixels!

So the rule is:
1. Find bounding box of non-zero pixels: [r_min, r_max] x [c_min, c_max].
2. Identify line rows and line cols:
A row r (between r_min and r_max) is a line row if the number of non-zero pixels in row r within [c_min, c_max] is clearly high (e.g. > (c_max - c_min + 1) / 2, or >= half).
A col c (between c_min and c_max) is a line col if the number of non-zero pixels in col c within [r_min, r_max] is > (r_max - r_min + 1) / 2.
3. For any line row r, fill every 0 between c_min and c_max with 2.
4. For any line col c, fill every 0 between r_min and r_max with 2.
All existing non-zero pixels remain their original color!
Let's double check if 2 overwrites anything: no, only 0s become 2.
And any cell that is on a line row or line col (within the bounding box) and currently 0 becomes 2!

Col 10 is a line from 1 to 9.
Together, they form a 3-row grid inside [1..9] x [2..10]!
Wait, what about the other vertical lines? There are none! Only row lines dividing it into horizontal strips!
Wait, why are there 2s in row 1, 4, 7, 9 and col 2, 10?
Because:
The bounding box of the shape is:
Row 1 to 9, Col 2 to 10!
And inside this bounding box, there are lines!
Which lines?
Rows that span from col 2 to col 10!
Cols that span from row 1 to row 9!
Wait, in Ex 1:
Bounding box: Row 2 to 8, Col 2 to 9!
Rows that span from col 2 to 9: Row 2 and Row 8!
Cols that span from row 2 to 8: Col 2, Col 5, Col 7, Col 9!
Wait! Col 5 spans from row 2 to 8!
Col 7 spans from row 2 to 8!

Col 5 and 7 are interior vertical lines!

Row 1 and 9 are the horizontal borders!
Row 4 and 7 are interior horizontal lines!
Col 2 and 10 are the vertical borders!
No interior vertical lines!
In Ex 3:
Bounding box:
Row 1 to 6, Col 1 to 6!
Row 1 and 6 are horizontal borders.
Col 1 and 6 are vertical borders.
No interior lines!
Just a single rectangle!

Wait, why are some lines considered lines?
Look at how the lines are drawn:
They are dashed/dotted lines of the same color!
A line is defined if:
Between the bounding box limits, there are pixels along that row/col.
Wait, could EVERY row or col that has pixels be a line?
No, in Ex 1:
Row 3 has pixels at col 2, 5, 7. But it is NOT completed into a line!
Why? Because row 3 is not a line!
Why is Row 4 in Ex 2 a line, but Row 3 in Ex 1 not a line?

Notice: The lines that are drawn have majority of pixels (or > 50% or >= threshold)?
Wait, look at row 7 in Ex 2:
It has 6 pixels, row 9 has 6 pixels, row 4 has 6 pixels, row 1 has 7 pixels.
All line rows have >= 6 pixels!
Other rows have at most 2 pixels!
In Ex 1:
Columns:

So the rule is:
1. Find bounding box of non-zero pixels: [r_min, r_max] x [c_min, c_max].
2. Identify line rows and line cols:
A row r (between r_min and r_max) is a line row if the number of non-zero pixels in row r within [c_min, c_max] is clearly high (e.g. > (c_max - c_min + 1) / 2, or >= half).
A col c (between c_min and c_max) is a line col if the number of non-zero pixels in col c within [r_min, r_max] is > (r_max - r_min + 1) / 2.
3. For any line row r, fill every 0 between c_min and c_max with 2.
4. For any line col c, fill every 0 between r_min and r_max with 2.
All existing non-zero pixels remain their original color!
Let's double check if 2 overwrites anything: no, only 0s become 2.
And any cell that is on a line row or line col (within the bounding box) and currently 0 becomes 2!
